t: A three-core RISC-V chip that can boot a tiny Linux and run small AI tasks.
steps: Buy a Pine64 Ox64 from the Pine64 store or a Sipeed M1s Dock kit from a seller such as Tindie.
Get a USB to serial adapter and a microSD card.
Download the Linux images from the openbouffalo buildroot_bouffalo GitHub page.
Install Bouffalo DevCube version 1.8.3, which the openbouffalo README asks for.
Wire the serial adapter to the board pins named in the README.
Hold the BOOT button and flash the low-load images and the Linux image.
Put the image on the microSD card and power the board.
Open a serial terminal on your computer and log in to Linux.
meta: Open Board. From $8. A few stores.
